title: Fixing Errors
instructions: Here's a secret: nobody writes perfect code the first time. Not beginners, not experts. Good programmers just read errors calmly and fix them.
When your code won't compile, gcc prints the error in the Output pane. Scary at first, but it usually tells you the line number and roughly what's wrong.
The code below has TWO bugs on purpose. Run it first, read the errors, then fix them.
- Capitalization matters. C is case-sensitive: main and Main are NOT the same. It must be lowercase main.
- Missing semicolon. Every statement ends with ;
task: Fix both bugs so the program compiles and prints:  Debugging is a skill.
hint:
Two fixes:
1) Change Main to main (lowercase m).
2) Add a semicolon ; at the end of the printf line.
